prompt: Don't use any tools. Now write 200 words about mountains, in 3 paragraphs.

text:
Mountains are some of the oldest and most imposing features on Earth. They form over millions of years as tectonic plates collide, forcing rock upward, or as volcanoes build layer after layer of cooled lava. The Himalayas are still rising, pushed higher each year as the Indian plate presses into Asia. Other ranges, like the Appalachians, were once as tall as the Himalayas and have since been worn into gentle, rounded ridges by wind, water, and ice.

Mountains shape the world around them. They pull moisture from passing air, so one side of a range is often lush while the other is dry desert. Glaciers and snowpack high on their slopes feed rivers that billions of people rely on for drinking water and farming. Their elevation creates distinct climate bands, so a single mountain can hold forests at its base, alpine meadows higher up, and bare rock and ice near the summit, each with its own plants and animals.

People have always been drawn to mountains. Many cultures treat them as sacred, the homes of gods or places close to the heavens. Climbers test themselves against their peaks, and hikers seek out the quiet and the long views. Standing on a summit, most people feel both small and more alive than usual.
